Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:10:1.hebrew: ודילמא הא לכתחילה הא דיעבד - כלומר, "לא יקח" — לאו שלא יהיו לו בהן קידושין דיעבד קאמר, אלא אזהרה שלא יקדשנה; ומיהו, אי קדיש — ניהוו קידושין, ואתא האי קרא אחרינא לומר דאין בה הויה כלל. ולעולם לבן קאמר, דכיון דאמר ולא פירש קרובים, אין לך להביא באיסור זה אלא האסור שבכולן, שקרוב מן הכל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:10:1.english: And perhaps this is ab initio [and] that is after the fact - That is to say: "A man shall not take" does not mean that betrothal with her does not take effect for him after the fact, but rather [it is] a prohibition that he may not betroth her; nevertheless, if he did betroth [her], let the betrothal take effect. And this other verse came to teach that with her there is no betrothal at all. And actually, it speaks of a son, for since it said ["to another man"] and did not specify relatives, you have [reason] to apply this prohibition only to the most forbidden among them all, who is closer than all [the others].

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:11:1.hebrew: מאחות אשה נפקא - דכתיב בה: "לא תקח" — לא תקדשנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:11:1.english: It is derived from a wife’s sister - For it is written concerning her: “You shall not take” (Leviticus 18:18) — you shall not betroth her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:11:2.english: Those liable to capital punishment - [Such as] one's father's wife, [which is punishable] by stoning.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:12:1.hebrew: אידי ואידי - "לא תקח", "והיתה לאיש אחר" — אימא: אידי ואידי באחות אשה; דכיון דאשכחן בה דאזהר עלה לכתחילה, איכא למימר דהדר כתב "והיתה לאיש אחר" למעוטי בעל אחותה, שאין לו בה הויה, אבל שאר קרובים, דלא אשכחן בהו אזהרת קיחה לכתחילה — לא קאמר: דיעבד לא נתפסו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:12:1.english: Both this and that - [The verses] “You shall not take” and “and she becomes another man’s wife” — say [that] both this and that [refer] to a wife’s sister. For since we find regarding her that [the Torah] prohibited her ab initio, one can say that it then wrote “and she becomes another man’s wife” to exclude her sister’s husband, [teaching] that he has no betrothal with her; but [as for] other relatives, regarding whom we do not find a prohibition of taking [in betrothal] ab initio, it did not say [that] after the fact [betrothal] does not take effect.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:12:2.english: Yes, it is indeed so - That one can derive [the law regarding] a wife’s sister alone.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:13:1.english: That we derive [them] from a wife’s sister - Through a binyan av [construct], via mah matzinu [“just as we find”].

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:14:1.hebrew: ה"ג: מה לאחות אשה שכן אין לה היתר במקום מצוה - כשאין לו בנים מאחיו המת, דילפינן בפ"ק דיבמות (דף ג:): נאמר כאן ״עליה בחייה״, ונאמר להלן ״יבמה יבא עליה״ — מה להלן במקום מצוה, אף כאן במקום מצוה, ואמר רחמנא: ״לא תקח״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:14:1.english: This is the correct version: “What is unique about a wife’s sister is that she has no permission in a situation of a mitzvah” - When he has no children from his deceased brother, as we derive in the first chapter of Yevamot (daf 3b): It is stated here, “upon her, in her lifetime,” and it is stated there, “her brother-in-law shall go in upon her” — just as there it is in a situation of a mitzvah, so too here the prohibition applies even in a situation of a mitzvah, and the Merciful One stated: “You shall not take.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:15:1.hebrew: מה להנך - לאחות אשה קאמר, שכן אין לה היתר בחיי אחותה האוסרת, שאפילו גירש אשתו, אחותה אסורה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:15:1.english: What [is unique] about these - [The Gemara] is speaking of a wife’s sister, for she has no [way of becoming] permitted during the lifetime of her sister who renders [her] forbidden, as even if he divorced his wife, her sister is forbidden.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:15:2.english: A married woman can become permitted during the lifetime of the one who renders her forbidden - For her husband permits her with a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:16:1.english: [Any] of these abominations - It is written in the section of forbidden relations [Leviticus 18:29].

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:1.english: “Any case” of the latter clause - [The clause where] there is betrothal and there is a transgression.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:2.hebrew: לאתויי גר שנשא ממזרת - לרבי יהודה, דיש עבירה, דהולד הולך אחר הפגום, דהוי ממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:2.english: To include a convert who married a mamzeret - According to Rabbi Yehuda, for there is a transgression, so the offspring follows the flawed [parent], such that [the child] is a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:3.english: As we said - To include an Israelite who married a ḥalalah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:4.hebrew: ואיזו זו דרישא כדאמרן - למעוטי דרבין או דרב דימי, וגר שנשא ממזרת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:4.english: And “In which case is this” of the first clause [is] as we said - To exclude [the ruling] of Ravin or of Rav Dimi, and a convert who married a mamzeret.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:5.hebrew: כל מקום דסיפא לאתויי מאי - היכא אשכחן תו יש קידושין ויש עבירה, הולד הולך אחר הפגום, בר מהני דקתני במתני':
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:1:5.english: “Any case” of the latter clause [serves] to include what? - Where do we find any further [case where] there is betrothal and there is a transgression, [and] the offspring follows the flawed [parent], besides those that are taught in the Mishnah?

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:4:1.hebrew: מאי באומות הלך אחר הזכר - למאי הילכתא יש להלך אחר הזכר כל זמן שלא נתגיירו, ומנ"ל דבתר זכר אזלינן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:4:1.english: What is [the meaning of]: “With regard to the nations, follow the male”? - For what halakha is one to follow the male as long as they have not converted, and from where do we [derive] that we follow the male?

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:6:1.hebrew: נתגיירו הלך אחר הפגום שבשניהם מאי היא - לענין עבדות ליכא למימר ״נתגיירו״, אלא לענין יוחסין. ולא מצינו חילוק בין אומה לאומה משנתגיירו אלא בעמוני ומצרי — שזה אסור לעולם, וזה עד דור שלישי. ופגום משני צדדים במאי משכחת לה, דקאמר ״הפגום שבשניהם״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:6:1.english: [If] they converted, follow the flawed [lineage] of the two of them — what is it? - With regard to slavery, one cannot say "they converted"; rather, [it must be] with regard to lineage. And we do not find a distinction between one nation and another nation once they convert, except in [the case of] an Ammonite and an Egyptian, as this one is forbidden forever and that one until the third generation. And in what [case] can you find [lineage that is] flawed from both sides, such that he says: "The flawed [one] of the two of them"?

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:6:2.hebrew: אילימא במצרי שנשא עמונית - וקאמר: הולד הולך אחר המצרי, ואסור עד דור שלישי, דאילו עמונית שריא לאלתר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:6:2.english: If we say, [it refers to] an Egyptian who married an Ammonite woman - And [the Gemara understands that he] is saying: The offspring follows the Egyptian, and is forbidden until the third generation, whereas an Ammonite woman is permitted immediately.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:6:3.hebrew: מאי פגום איכא - בצד האם. דקאמר ״נתגיירו״, אתרוייהו קאי — לשון רבים — ומשמע דבמידי דמשכחת ביה פגם לגבי תרוייהו קאמר, והכא גבי אם ליכא פגם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:6:3.english: What flaw is there - [Meaning,] on the mother’s side. For when [Rabbi Yoḥanan] said, “they converted,” it refers to both of them — [using] plural phrasing — which implies that he was speaking of a case where one finds a flaw regarding both of them, and here, regarding the mother, there is no flaw.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:7:1.hebrew: מצרי ואדומי - עשה בהם נקבות כזכרים, כדאמר ביבמות (דף עז:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:7:1.english: An Egyptian and an Edomite - [Scripture] made females among them like males, as it says in Yevamot (77b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:7:2.hebrew: אי זכר - הולד — שדיא בתר עמוני, ואיסור זכרים שבו לעולם; ולא אמרי': שדיא בתר מצרית, ויהא דור שלישי מותר. ואי נקבה היא — שדייה בתר מצרית, ולא בתר עמוני למשרייה לדידה משום "ולא עמונית", אלא בנה יהא מותר שהוא שלישי; דאמר קרא (דברים כ״ג:ט׳): "להם" — הלך אחר פסולן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:7:2.english: If [the child] is a male - The offspring — cast him after the Ammonite [father], and the prohibition of males that applies to him is forever; and we do not say: Cast him after the Egyptian [mother], and [thus] the third generation would be permitted. And if it is a female — cast her after the Egyptian [mother], and not after the Ammonite [father] to permit her on account of [the rule] "and not an Ammonite woman"; rather, [only] her son will be permitted, as he is [of the] third [generation]. For Scripture states (Deuteronomy 23:9): "[...unto] them" — follow their disqualification.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:8:1.hebrew: מנה"מ - דאין קידושין תופסין בחייבי כריתות. אבל הולד ממזר — נפקא לן מלא יקח איש את אשת אביו ולא יגלה כנף אביו, וסמיך ליה "לא יבא ממזר", ומוקמינן לה ביבמות (דף מט.) בשומרת יבם של אביו, שהיא לו אשת אחי אביו, שהיא בכרת. ומהכא ילפינן לה ביבמות בפרק החולץ (יבמות דף מה:) דכל שאין לה עליו קידושין, הולד ממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:8:1.english: From where are these matters [derived]? - That betrothal does not take effect with those liable to excision; however, [that] the offspring is a mamzer is derived by us from: “A man shall not take his father’s wife, nor uncover his father’s skirt” (Deuteronomy 23:1), and juxtaposed to it: “A mamzer shall not enter” (Deuteronomy 23:3). And we establish it in Yevamot (49a) as [referring to] a woman awaiting levirate marriage with his father, who is to him his father’s brother’s wife, which is [punishable] by excision. And from here we derive it in Yevamot in chapter Hacholetz (Yevamot 45b), that in any case where she cannot join in betrothal with him, the offspring is a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:8:2.hebrew: ומטו בה - יש מטים בדבר זה לומר שבשם ר' ינאי נאמר. ורב אחא בריה דרבא אמר: לאו משום רבי ינאי מטו בה, אלא משום רבי יוסי הגלילי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:8:2.english: And they traced it - There are those who incline regarding this matter, to say that it was stated in the name of Rabbi Yannai. And Rav Aḥa, the son of Rava, said: It was not in the name of Rabbi Yannai that they traced it, but rather in the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:8:3.hebrew: לאיש אחר - שהוא אחר אצלה, ולא שהוא קרובה. והיתה — לשון קידושין הוא, שהיתה לו בהן לאשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:8:3.english: To another man - That he is another [i.e., unrelated] to her, and not that he is her relative. “And she becomes” — this is an expression of betrothal, [meaning] that through them she became a wife to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:9:1.hebrew: לבן - בן בעלה, אבל שאר קרובות לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:9:1.english: To a son - Her husband's son, but other female relatives [are] not [forbidden]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:9:2.hebrew: לא יקח - לא יהא לך בה ליקוחין, שאין קידושין תופסין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 67b:9:2.english: He shall not take - There shall not be for you [any] taking with her, [meaning] that betrothal does not take effect.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 67b:8:1.hebrew: מנא הני מילי - נראה דלא בעי מה"מ דהולד ממזר, דהא ביבמות (דף מט.) מוכח ליה מלא יגלה כנף אביו, וסמיך ליה לא יבא ממזר, ומוקמי לה ביבמות (שם) בשומרת יבם של אביו, שהיא לו אשת אחי אביו, שהיא בכרת; אלא בעי: מנא לן דאין קידושין תופסין בהן? וקשה: דמאי בעי? הלא הדבר פשוט בכל הגמרא דקידושין לא תפסי, דהא בהא תליא! דכיון דהוי ממזר מחייבי כריתות, לא תפסי קידושין — דהא ר"ע הוא דאמר (שם) דאין קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין, ולא ידעינן אלא משום דשמעינן ליה לר"ע דאמר יש ממזר מחייבי לאוין, וכיון דיש ממזר — דין הוא דלא תפסי בה קידושין; והכי נמי אמרינן בשמעתין: הכל מודים בבא על הנדה שאין הולד ממזר, דהא תפסי בה קידושין — אלמא דהא בהא תליא! ואור"י: דאין ה"נ, דכלל זה אמת אליבא דר"ע; והכא בעי אליבא דרבי יהושע, דאמר (שם): אין ממזר מחייבי לאוין [וכריתות] אלא מחייבי מיתות ב"ד, ואפ"ה מודה דאין קידושין תופסין בחייבי כריתות, כדאמר (הכל מודים) שאין קידושין תופסין באחותו, אלמא דדבר פשוט הוא לכ"ע; ואליבא דרבי יהושע בעי גמרא: מנלן דלא תפסי קידושין בחייבי כריתות:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 67b:8:1.english: "From where are these matters [derived]?" - It appears that [the Gemara] is not asking: From where are these matters [derived] that the offspring is a mamzer? For in Yevamot (49a), it derives this from "He shall not uncover his father's skirt" (Deuteronomy 23:1), and juxtaposed to it is: "A mamzer shall not enter" (Deuteronomy 23:3), and they establish it in Yevamot (ibid.) as referring to a woman awaiting yibbum with his father, who is [forbidden] to him as his father's brother's wife, which is [punishable] by karet. Rather, [the Gemara] is asking: From where do we [derive] that betrothal does not take effect with them? And it is difficult: for what is [the Gemara] asking? Is this matter not simple throughout the entire Gemara that betrothal does not take effect, since this depends on that? For since the offspring from those liable to karet is a mamzer, betrothal does not take effect, as it is Rabbi Akiva who says (there) that betrothal does not take effect with those liable to negative commandments, and we only know [this] because we heard of Rabbi Akiva that he says there is a mamzer from those liable to negative commandments, and since there is a mamzer, it is logical that betrothal does not take effect with her; and so too we say in our sugya: Everyone agrees regarding one who has relations with a menstruating woman [niddah] that the offspring is not a mamzer, because betrothal takes effect with her — evidently, this depends on that! And Ri says: Indeed so, that this rule is true according to Rabbi Akiva; but here [the Gemara] is asking according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who says (there): There is no mamzer from those liable to negative commandments [or karet], but only from those liable to court-imposed death penalties, and even so, he concedes that betrothal does not take effect with those liable to karet, as [the Gemara] says "(Everyone agrees) that betrothal does not take effect with his sister" — evidently, it is a simple matter to all; and according to Rabbi Yehoshua, the Gemara is asking: From where do we [derive] that betrothal does not take effect with those liable to karet?
